summary: Wenzhou University study of how evaluated heuristic programs are converted into GRPO rewards when a small (7B) LLM is post-trained online inside the CALM co-evolutionary automatic heuristic design (AHD) loop for combinatorial optimisation (TSP, CVRP, OBP, OP). It compares four reward mappings against a frozen generator with search held fixed. On TSP with Qwen2.5-7B over three seeds, all trained arms beat the frozen generator at a 500-group horizon, but none dominates, and under timing-derived budgets online updating does not reliably beat simply running more frozen search.

claims.claim: Every trained reward mapping improves live search over the frozen generator at a common 500-group horizon.
claims.evidence: Table 2 / Fig. 3(b): final best -6.209 (Native), -6.204 (Factorized), -6.196 (Tail-weighted) vs -6.233 (Frozen) on TSP, three seeds each; validity 85-96% vs 60.85%. One task and one model in the efficacy cohort.

claims.claim: No reward mapping uniformly dominates; mappings trade validity, valid-only performance and contextual improvement yield.
claims.evidence: Table 2 and §6: Native has best valid-only performance, Tail-weighted best improve yield but lower validity; paired seed directions are mixed.

claims.claim: Online updating does not reliably beat extra frozen search under resource-matched budgets.
claims.evidence: §6: Native and Factorized each beat the time-anchored Frozen prefix in only 1 of 3 seeds (mean diffs -0.0113 and +0.0035); budgets are timing-derived anchors, not exact time matches.

patterns.note: Online RL of the program generator beats a frozen generator at equal horizon but not reliably at matched compute. The domain is optimisation-heuristic search, not software-engineering agents, so this does not carry over to coding-agent fine-tuning.

methodology.sample: Live efficacy cohort: TSP x Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct x 3 seeds x 500 groups (2,000 completions per run); mechanism audits on 4 tasks; matched updates on 2 tasks x 2 model families, one seed each.
methodology.baselines: Frozen CALM (no updates) and released Native CALM reward; no other AHD systems by design.
methodology.models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct plus a second 7B family for mechanism probes; rank-32 LoRA.
methodology.variance: Seed-level mean +- SD over three seeds; no significance tests.
methodology.ablations: Reward mapping is the manipulated factor; population-reset restarts and time-anchored frozen search for attribution.

standards.peer_review: Preprint (arXiv comment: '18 pages, including supplementary material. Preprint').
standards.artifacts: arXiv source package only; experiment code, configs and raw records are described as retained but not included.
standards.preregistration: Internally pre-specified frozen-search budgets; no public registry.

biases.detail: Three seeds on one task-model cell for all efficacy claims.
Live efficacy cohort uses only Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
Code and run records not publicly released.
Automatic heuristic design for combinatorial optimisation; not software development with agents or its human side.

verdict_reason: Off-topic for this KB: it studies RL reward construction for evolving TSP/CVRP heuristics, not software development with LLM agents or developer knowledge discovery. The experiment is careful (three seeds, held-fixed search, time-anchored frozen baseline, restrained claims), but it carries no evidence for any harness decision the team faces.
applicability: None for the discovery and onboarding harness. The team also does not post-train models (model choice belongs to the agent host), so even the general RL-for-code insight does not transfer.
